title: Aligned Score Row
statement:
Print one row of a score table, with the columns lined up.

The input is one line with a name (a single word of 1 to 10 letters) and a whole-number score from 0 to 99999, separated by a space. Print one line of exactly 15 characters:

- the name left-aligned in a column 10 characters wide, padded with spaces on the right
- then the score right-aligned in a column 5 characters wide, padded with spaces on the left

A name of exactly 10 letters gets no padding, so it touches the score. A score of 5 digits fills its column.

Input:

```text
Ana 95
```

Expected output:

```text
Ana          95
```
hints: Format strings can give each value a width, so you do not have to count spaces yourself.
One column pads on the right and the other pads on the left. Many languages mark left alignment with `-` or `<`.

python.solution:
def format_row(name: str, score: int) -> str:
    return f"{name:<10}{score:>5}"


name, score = input().split()
print(format_row(name, int(score)))
